documentation.rationale: Both halves are present but incomplete. On identity and terms: a chassis number, no reserve, and an NH registration plus a dealer-assigned MA title. On maintenance: a named-shop top-end invoice of ~$12k, service records and a cold-start video. Missing are the invoice's itemization (studs and tensioners), leakdown figures, COA/number photos, structural lift photos and any history report.

condition.rationale: The rebuilt top end ~3-4k miles ago is a real positive, and the paint and interior photograph well. Against that, several items are observed: driver door resistance, exposed stereo wiring, and surface corrosion on the heat exchangers and underside hardware. The car has 148k miles and no compression or leakdown data. Structural condition is unexamined.

price_value.rationale: No fair-value estimate or sold comps are supplied. The current $12k bid is early, and a high-mile SC coupe with a documented top end typically finishes well above it. At an expected market hammer, with open questions on studs, rust and smog compliance, value is roughly market-level with downside risk.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual with a strong point of view, and SCs resell easily within 6-24 months. However, the likely hammer sits above the $10k-$19k ideal band. A 47-year-old air-cooled car with a CA smog question and a $3k-$8k typical catch-up is less 'reliable bridge' than the brief wants.

logistics.rationale: Barrington, NH is across the country, PPI access is not stated, and the auction closes in about four days. The seller is cooperative, so a local Porsche specialist PPI may be arrangeable. CA smog feasibility is unconfirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A Guards Red SC coupe with a 915 manual, sunroof and Fuchs wheels is a desirable, classic spec. It is tempered by a non-original interior treatment (plaid panels, leatherette), an aftermarket shifter, MOMO wheel and active exhaust, and no proven matching numbers.

evidence.mission_note: It satisfies the manual, point-of-view brief and resells easily. However, it is a 47-year-old air-cooled car needing a CA smog pass and catch-up work, and the likely hammer sits above the ideal $10k-$19k band. It is a stretch as a low-risk bridge rather than a natural one.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 1979 911SC coupe with a 915 manual, chassis 9119201583, 148k indicated miles and a Nov 2022 top-end overhaul by a named Massachusetts shop. A ~$12k invoice for that work is posted, but its contents were not examined here. Observed issues are a disclosed driver-door opening resistance, exposed console wiring, and surface corrosion on the heat exchangers and underside hardware in the one underbody photo. An unanswered bidder question asks whether the catalytic converter is non-original, which matters alongside the 2025 M&K exhaust because a 1979 car is not CA smog-exempt. The seller confirms no compression or leakdown testing was done. Ownership rests on an NH registration plus a dealer-assigned MA title of unknown brand status. Still open are head-stud and tensioner work, structural rust in the front pan and kidney bowls, numbers matching and tire age. The only internal inconsistency is the leather versus leatherette description of the seats.
evidence.next_action: Before the Oct 27 close, message the seller asking for the itemized Auto Sport Inc invoice page, the catalytic converter and exhaust CARB details, and lift photos. In parallel, contact an NH-area Porsche specialist to see whether a PPI with leakdown can be done before bidding.
